texts.preamble: Northern Railway vs A-1) Mohd. Ahad on 27 March, 2017 In The Court Of Sh. Ashu Garg, Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii (New Delhi), Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 169/04 (40298/16) Unique Case Id No. 02403R0347482004 Date of Institution: 08.09.2004 Date of reserving judgement: 27.03.2017 Date of pronouncement: 27.03.2017 In re: Northern Railway through Food Inspector Baroda House, New Delhi ... Complainant versus A-1) Mohd. Ahad S/o Mohd. Illyas, R/o. 461, Block-D, Jahangir Puri, Delhi-33 A-2) Amrish Kumar Regional Manager, Hpmpc Limited. Himachal Cold Storage, C-1,2,3, Lawrence Road, Delhi-110035. A-3) H.P.M.C Limited Nigam Vihar, Simla-2, Himachal Pradesh ... Accused persons Cc No. 169/04 Page 1 of 9 Judgment:
texts.facts: 1. The present is a complaint filed by Northern Railway under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (PFA Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. The accused no. 1 is stated to be the salesman of Himachal Pradesh Horticultural Product Marketing and Processing Corporation Limited (HPMC) stall at New Concrose, Paharganj Side, New Delhi Railway Station, from where the food article, that is, "Ditto (Mango Drink)" was lifted for sampling. Accused no. 2 is the Regional Manager of accused no.3 HPMC from which the product was supplied to the accused no. 1. Northern Railway vs A-1) Mohd. Ahad on 27 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159045640/ 1 2. As per the complaint, on 24.08.2003, Food Inspector (FI) Jagjeet Singh found the accused no. 1 conducting the business at his stall and having stored "Ditto (Mango Drink)" for sale to passengers/public for human consumption in sealed tetra packets of 200 ml each. He disclosed his identity and expressed intention to lift the sample. Two Health Inspectors Khem Singh and Ramji Prasad were also joined as witnesses, when no public persons agreed. The FI issued notice in Form VI and lifted six sealed tetra packs of "Ditto (Mango Drink)" as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot including panchnama. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with LHA/Chief Medical Superintendent, Northern Railway. Vide report dated 09.09.2003, the PA found the sample to be misbranded on the ground that the label was without declaration of addition of colour. Upon receipt of report, the LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by FI. It was found that the food article was supplied by accused no.3 HPMC Limited. Further, accused no. 2 was found to be Regional Manager and not one Sh. Prem Pradeep as told by the vendor / accused no.1 at the time of sampling. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Chief Medical Director. The complaint was then filed in the court on 08.09.2004 alleging violation of Rule 24 of PFA Rules as punishable section 7/16 of PFA Act. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused persons were summoned vide order dated 08.09.2004. Accused persons appeared in response to the summons. 4. Based on the PA report, notice of accusation under Section 251 CrPC was framed against all the accused persons vide order dated 17.12.2009 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) of PFA Act, being violation of Rule 24 of PFA Rules, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 5. At the trial, the prosecution examined two witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 Ramji Prasad and PW-2 Khem Singh were the Health Inspectors who deposed about the proceedings conducted by the FI on 24.08.2003 and narrated the steps undertaken by the FI during the sample proceedings. They also proved the necessary documents including the notice Ex. PW-1/A, vendor receipt Ex. PW-1/B and Panchnama Ex. PW- 1/C. These witnesses were not cross-examined on behalf of accused no.1. During cross examination on behalf of accused no.2 and 3, they denied that they were not present in the proceedings or that no attempt was made to join public witnesses. 6. At this stage, it is pertinent to note that no authorized person had been appearing on behalf of the complainant for a very long time. The complainant Food Inspector Jagjeet Singh neither appeared in the court ever, nor was examined as a witness, nor was even cited as a witness. Record shows that Ld. Counsel Sh. C. K. Sharma appeared as counsel for the complainant last on 03.03.2015. Subsequently, on few occasions, the presence of Ld. SPP for Complainant (Ld. SPP appears in other matter under PFA Act on behalf of the complainant therein i.e. Department of PFA / Food Safety Department). Technically speaking, the said Ld. SPP appearing in other cases could not have appeared in this case as he was never authorized to represent the complainant Northern Railway. Northern Railway vs A-1) Mohd. Ahad on 27 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159045640/ 2 Record further shows that Sh. Vinay Kumar, Advocate had appeared as proxy counsel on behalf of the complainant on 31.03.2016 and 21.07.2016. On 30.09.2016, he stated that he was only appearing as a proxy counsel as he had not been authorized by the complainant department to represent it as a counsel. The complainant was therefore granted one more opportunity to appoint an AR and to authorized any counsel to represent it. However, on subsequent dates, neither any AR nor any authorized counsel appeared on behalf of the complainant. When the matter was at the stage of recording of S.A, vide order dated 30.09.2016, this court also pointed out that the FI who had conducted the investigation and filed the complaint had neither been examined nor his name appeared in the list of witnesses. The said Sh. Vinay Kumar appearing as proxy counsel sought time to take instructions in this regard. But none appeared for the complainant thereafter. 7. As such, statements of the accused persons under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 27.03.2017 wherein they denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Accused no. 1 stated that he was only a servant and that the licensee was one Smt. Savitri Jain. Accused no. 2 (also representing accused no. 3) denied the sample proceedings as they were not present at the spot. He however stated that he was not the nominee of the company and was not responsible or in charge of the affairs of company pertaining to the labelling declarations. They chose not to lead evidence in defence. 8. It is in these circumstances, Ld. Defence Counsel has submitted that there is nothing on record to show that accused persons were the persons incharge of or responsible to the company HPMC Limited for conduct of its business affairs. It is pointed out that the food inspector who had conducted the sample proceedings, carried out the investigation and filed the complaint has not been examined on record and therefore, none of the investigative steps have been proved on record. 9. On the other hand, as already stated, the complainant stopped participating in the court proceedings. Even Ld. Proxy Counsel stopped appearing. There was no representation on behalf of the complainant despite several opportunities. However, instead of dismissing the matter in default of appearance, this court proceeded with the matter on merits of the case as the evidence was already closed.
